t: How Instagram received Nate Soares's caveman-speak explainer of AI risk
d: We coded 1,534 Instagram comments on a one-minute reel by Nate Soares of the Machine Intelligence Research Institute (MIRI). Most commenters accepted the argument. Many said it was already too late, and almost nobody asked what to do.

t: "Please honor commit": how the OpenAI agent-swarm story landed with the audience most likely to believe it
d: We coded 1,245 YouTube comments on the Dwarkesh Podcast's interview with METR's Ajeya Cotra about the OpenAI agent-swarm incident. The audience accepted the danger, joked about it, praised the messenger, and had no idea what to do next.

t: "Neither company is acting responsibly": how X received Jacob Coxon's resignation from Anthropic
d: We coded 2,480 replies to a former Anthropic researcher's resignation thread on X. The audience split almost evenly, and the most-liked reply didn't engage with his argument at all.

Common Signals helps AI communicators know which messages actually work: research, tools, training and workshops for anyone talking about AI.

Common Signals studies how the people who see messages about AI respond to them. Our theory of change explains how this work fits our wider aims. This page describes the method our studies share, so anyone can check, criticise or repeat the work. Each study publishes its own figures, codebook and dataset.

t: OpenAI and shut? What an independent report did to the marketing-stunt argument
d: We compared Reddit comments on the OpenAI and Hugging Face incident before and after METR and Redwood Research published an independent investigation. Afterwards, fewer people called it a stunt and more accepted it happened. The ones still calling it a stunt got harder to shift.

t: "A problem they created": how a news audience received the accountability version of the OpenAI and Hugging Face incident
d: We coded 322 YouTube comments on Amanpour and Company's interview with Heidy Khlaaf, who argues the "rogue AI" story is the wrong one. Most of the audience agreed with her, got angrier as the thread aged, and asked for regulation without being prompted.
